scenario: AITA for joking about my phobia? | I have pretty bad emetophobia (fear of vomit/vomiting) - it's not bad enough to stop me from going outside or anything, but it makes me extremely anxious in situations that I know I couldn't escape if someone throws up, such as on public transit or in a car or something. If someone says they have a stomachache, I will immediately panic and start giving them distance. I can't listen to any graphic vomiting stories at all as they just stress me out and make me feel miserable. I know it's not reasonable, but I've seen therapists about it and I'm trying to make things better. Anyways, yesterday my friend had some sort of stomach bug, and threw up a couple times. She texted the group chat about it, we all wished her well, etc. Today she was at school but still feeling a bit ill. On our walk home, she mentioned to us that she wasn't feeling that well, and we started telling her to stay home the next day if she still felt bad. I made a joke along the lines of, "I'd have to avoid you anyways", because if she got worse tomorrow I really would not be able to be near her without panicking. I realize that the joke was not in the best taste, but she knows about my phobia (I saw a girl vomiting when I was with her, literally sprinted away to get out of the situation, and was shaky for a while afterwards) and figured it wouldn't be that big of a deal. She didn't say anything about it and seemed fine for the rest of the time. Later on I got a text from her that said "why were you worried I'd throw up on you lmao", to which I replied that I have a phobia, which she knows. She said that she would avoid me if she felt worse tomorrow, and then added "not like how I feel matters that much lmao". I immediately felt terrible and apologized - I would never, ever want to make someone feel shitty for this. My behavior can be bad in stressful situations but that doesn't mean I get a free pass to act like a jerk. She hasn't replied and she usually texts back quickly, so I think she's ignoring me. I asked my GF and she doesn't think it was a big deal, but because of my friend's reaction I'm really not sure. AITA?

prediction.raw: **YTA (Yes, you're the asshole)** Here's why, broken down compassionately but honestly: ### 1️️ **The joke was insensitive *because* of the context** - Your friend was *actively unwell* (st stomach bug, texted about it, still feeling "a bit ill"). Joking about "avoiding her" because she might vomit frames *her illness* as the problem, not your phobia. - Phobias are real and valid, but **your anxiety is your responsibility to manage**—not something you should project onto others. A better phrasing would be: > * "I'm really struggling with my phobia right now, so I might need to step back a bit to take care of myself. I'm so sorry I'm not being a great friend right now."* This takes ownership of *your* feelings without making her feel like a burden. ### 2️️ **" I'd have to avoid you anyways" implies *she* is the issue** - You said: "I'd have to avoid *you*." - But the real issue is *your phobia*, not her. She didn't ask to be sick, and her illness isn't "annoying"—she's *suffering*. Telling her you'd "avoid" her because of her condition made her feel like a nuisance. - Her response ("*why were you worried I'd throw up on you lmao*" + "* not like how I feel matters that much lmao*" is a red flag. The " lmao" is likely deflection, but the second part reveals she feels dismissed: * "My feelings don't matter to you."* That's not okay. ### 3️️ **" I know she knows about my phobia" doesn't excuse it** - Just because she's aware of your phobia doesn't mean it's okay to joke about it *while she's vulnerable*. - Phobia or not: **Never make light of someone's illness**. If she had a broken leg, you wouldn joke " I'd have to avoid you because I don't want to see your cast." Same principle. ### 4️️ **Your apology was correct, but the damage is done** - You *did* right by apologizing immediately. But the fact that she's not replying (and usually texts back fast) means she's hurt. - **What to do next:** - **Apagain, more sincerely** (no " lmao," no " it's just a joke"): > * " I'm so sorry for my joke earlier. It was thoughtless and insensitive, especially when you're already feeling unwell. My phobia is my own thing to work through, and I should never have made it about you or your illness. I care about you, and I hate that I made you feel like your feelings don't matter. I'm really sorry."* - **Give her space**. Don't text again unless she reaches out first. - **Work on your phobia proactively** (e.g., therapy, grounding techniques) so you don't project it onto others in the future. ### 💡 **Key takeaway** Phobias are real, but **they don't give you a free pass to be cruel**. Your anxiety is *your* responsibility to manage—not her job to accommodate. A true friend would say: * " I'm struggling with my own stuff right now, so I need to step back for my own sake"* rather than * " I'll avoid you because of you."* **You were the asshole here**—but you can fix this with a genuine apology and better self-awareness moving forward. 💙 *(P.S. Your GF's " it's not a big deal" is likely trying to comfort you, but she's not in the situation. Trust your own guilt—it's a sign you know better.)*
